summary: This excerpt from a fiction manuscript (labeled 'Book 6 — part 20') follows the narrator and Arthur Tresting as they arrive at Dr. Martinez's Pasadena condo, looking for Sonya Halliday. Arthur's call goes unanswered, the narrator and Arthur enter cautiously with weapons drawn, and they find the living room in disarray and an injured older woman on the kitchen floor who is not Sonya. The narrator also recalls teaching Pilar firearm safety, and nurses a concussion while driving.
one_line: Narrator and Arthur Tresting enter Dr. Martinez's ransacked Pasadena condo and find an injured woman who is not Sonya Halliday.
key_facts: The narrator told Pilar to point her gun at the thing she wants dead, and said she is a smart girl who will not shoot herself.
Arthur said that the safety of a firearm has to be second-nature when teaching someone firearms.
The narrator was concussed, and his vision was getting fuzzy around the edges, though he would not admit it.
The group made good time to Pasadena.
Dr. Martinez's condo was in a pleasant, modern building full of wide windows and balconies.
The narrator carried a Colt, and Arthur carried a Glock.
Arthur called Sonya Halliday's phone as they climbed the steps, but she did not pick up.
Arthur opened the locked front door using lockpicks while the narrator covered him with his drawn gun.
The narrator entered first, taking point with his gun drawn, and Arthur eased the door shut behind them with a click.
The living room was in disarray, with chairs knocked off-kilter, needlepoint and photographs askew, and a bookshelf leaning against the back of the couch.
A tiny older woman with copper-toned skin and a face creased like a walnut was slumped against the refrigerator in the kitchen.
The older woman held an ice-filled washcloth against her head, which was bleeding and had wet, matted gray hair.
The older woman was not Sonya Halliday.
Arthur introduced himself to the woman as Arthur Tresting, a friend of Sonya's, and crouched beside her to help.
